Implementation details:

### Activities menu overlay
Full-screen overlay `.activities-overlay` with header, 3 cards:
- 01 · DISASSEMBLY BAY "Take it apart. Put it back." with icon
- 02 · SCRAP RUN "Slice crates, droids & salvage" (Fruit Ninja)
- 03 · TRAINING DUEL "Coming soon" locked.

Cards with mini illustrations maybe CSS/emoji-ish. Use inline SVG icons for consistency. Each card has label, title, desc, status, button.

Open on click of activities button. Close on X/Escape/backdrop. Body class dialog-active maybe activities-active.

### Disassembly activity
Full-screen overlay with canvas rendering the current saber. Should be a 3D Three.js scene. Reuse model? Need separate scene + renderer. Building the saber requires selected options; we can temporarily build model into activity scene. Existing rebuildSaber builds into global model tied to saberRoot. Could construct a clone of the current model and split by component groups. But existing model is flat group; parts are not separated by category. For disassembly animation, we need "all the parts float out". We can group meshes by vertical y position into logical components: blade, emitter, switch/upper barrel, grip, pommel. Or better, we can create a separate build function for the activity that builds parts into groups. Duplicating entire saber builder would be huge. Alternative: use model.clone(true) then partition meshes by bounding box y coordinate into 5-7 bands; each band assigned to a group; animate groups outward radially. That satisfies "all the parts float out".

Even better: add invisible userData.part tags in rebuildSaber? We could modify rebuildSaber to tag each mesh with part category based on where it's created. That's a big edit but doable via wrapper: create helper `part(groupName)`? There are dozens of addMesh calls. Could tag based on y ranges post-build by geometry positions. Simpler and robust: after cloning, traverse meshes, compute world Y; assign to component based on Y thresholds relative to model coordinate:
- blade parts: y > 1.12 (blade, emitter top maybe)
- emitter: .55–1.12
- upper barrel/switch: .15–.55
- grip: -.38–.15
- pommel: < -.38
- crystal: near .89.

But for a cool explode effect, bands along Y and also angle offsets. All meshes in a band move together; parts float out in ring patterns. Blade should maybe retract/ignite off? We'll force blade off for disassembly (the hilt only) or keep blade? "disassembling the lightsaber you build, so it float in the center like usual" implies current saber. Press disassemble all parts float out. Blade probably should power down during disassembly. Let's make blade extinguish on disassemble (blade group retract upward/scale) and rebuild as hilt parts. Simpler: clone only hilt (blade off) by temporarily setting bladeIgnited=false and rebuild? But rebuildSaber affects main scene. We can build in the activity by temporarily toggling global state, calling rebuildSaber? Hmm rebuildSaber also syncs auction etc. Not ideal but workable: save bladeIgnited, set false, rebuildSaber(), clone model, restore. But model global changes; restore after. Actually activity can simply clone `model` as-is and hide meshes with bladeGlow/userData? For blade, detect meshes above y 1.15 that are additive/transparent. If blade ignited, we can fade them out quickly.

Better: create dedicated activity scene with its own clone. We need to render the hilt in "floating in center like usual". We'll create scene with lighting similar to main. Copy current model (which may include blade) and clone. For part bands, assign each mesh to one of e.g. 7 groups by Y. Animate each group from home position to exploded position with easing, with slight rotation. On assemble, reverse.

To make it feel like parts, we can define explode targets: each band moves to radius ring at angles around center. Also stagger delays. For individual pieces within a band, maybe distribute individually: each mesh gets its own target computed from its home position direction plus outward offset, and band-based vertical spread. That would look like every part floats out separately. "all the parts float out" — yes, individual meshes floating apart is nice.

Approach: traverse clone meshes; for each mesh, store its current local position/quaternion/scale; assign target = home + outward offset. Outward direction based on its angular position around Y plus a bit of Y separation. For blade meshes (long), hide or treat specially. We can compute bounding box center in model local coordinates. If y > 1.15 and material additive -> blade; fade them out and not include in explode. Hmm blade core extends from 1.14 to 4.7. During disassemble, the blade should retract. We can scale blade group along y? Simpler: when opening activity, build clone with blade turned off. We can temporarily build a hilt-only model: save selected/blade state, set bladeIgnited = false, rebuildSaber(), clone, then restore and rebuild. That's synchronous and safe. But rebuildSaber touches auction scene; okay.

Actually easier: write a helper `makeActivitySaber()` that temporarily switches blade off, calls rebuildSaber, clones model, restores, and calls rebuildSaber. It will cost some milliseconds but fine.

Hmm, but rebuildSaber syncs auction & resizes; no big deal.

Then partition each mesh by Y:
- y >= 0.55: emitter assembly
- 0.12–0.55: upper barrel/switch
- -0.42–0.12: grip
- < -0.42: pommel
Also crystal at y .89 in emitter group. Fine.

But there are many small meshes (knurl studs) — each will fly individually, looks like a cloud of parts. Great.

Explode targets: for each mesh, direction = normalize(home x, home z) if radial distance > 0.02 else random unit vector; target radius = 1.2 + groupIndex*0.2 plus slight; target Y = homeY + (groupIndex - 2)*0.9 maybe spread vertically. Add per-mesh jitter. Also rotate target random Euler.

Animate with tween via JS in render loop: store `explodeProgress` 0..1, with spring/ease. Each mesh position = lerp(home, target, ease), rotation = lerp(homeQuat, targetQuat, ease). Stagger per mesh delay: use local progress = clamp((progress - delay*0.3)/0.7). Group delay by index.

Buttons: DISASSEMBLE / ASSEMBLE toggle. Status text "9 COMPONENTS · 38 PIECES". Progress indicator. Also a "power down" hint. The initial state has floating idle rotation like main.

We need the overlay canvas size and render loop. Use separate renderer; render only when overlay open. Add to main animate or its own rAF. I'll render inside main animate loop when open, similar to auction.

Also allow drag rotate? Nice-to-have. Implement pointer drag on activity canvas to rotate.

### Slicer game (Fruit Ninja style)
Need a complete playable mini-game. Implement on 2D canvas (simpler and performant) with a star wars salvage theme:
- Objects launched from bottom of canvas in parabolic arcs: crates (brown boxes), battle droids (tan B1 droid silhouette), astromech? "random stuff from star wars" — e.g., barrels, protocol droid heads, stormtrooper helmets, probe droids, thermal detonators (bomb = don't slice?).
- Player swipes with mouse/touch; blade trail drawn as glowing line. If swipe intersects object, it splits into two halves that fly apart with particle sparks, score +.
- Bombs: thermal detonators — slicing loses a life / ends game? Classic fruit ninja has bombs. Add 3 lives and "avoid thermal detonators". Could do lives.
- Timer 60 seconds; score; combo multiplier; best score in localStorage.
- Missing objects (fall off screen) loses a life (or no penalty for crates? classic loses life). Keep 3 misses allowed.
- Game over panel with score, best, restart, back to activities.
- Slicing detection: maintain pointer trail points with timestamps; each frame check segment intersection between recent swipe segment and object bounding circle. Or simpler, on pointer move, check distance from pointer segment to object center < radius+blade width. That's robust.
- Draw objects with canvas 2D vector art: crate with panels, droid with head/body/arms, helmet, barrel, probe droid. Add half-split pieces when sliced: draw two halves clipped? We can spawn two "half" objects with clip paths rotated. Simpler: on slice, create debris pieces: two rectangles/circles of the object's base color flying apart, plus spark particles. Could draw two halves using canvas clip on original object art with a diagonal cut. That's more work but doable: function drawObjectArt(ctx, type, size) then for halves, clip half-plane and draw full art rotated/translated. Nice.

- crate: wooden/metal supply crate (brown), 70px, points 10
- droid: B1 battle droid (tan), 60x80, points 15

- barrel: canister, 50x70, 10
- probe: black sphere with antennae, 50, 25
- detonator: dark sphere with red blinking light, slicing = penalty (lose life, screen flash) points -? Avoid.

Spawn logic: every 700-1200ms launch 1-3 objects with gravity. Launch from bottom with vx toward center, vy upward; gravity 900 px/s². They arc up and fall. Object rotates. Slice when swipe crosses.

Canvas resolution: use devicePixelRatio capped 2, size to container.

Use pointer events. Trail: array of points {x,y,t}; draw fading trail with gradient glow (lime/white), lineWidth taper. A "blade" cursor? Add a crosshair maybe. On pointerdown start slicing, pointermove add points. But desktop users may just move mouse without pressing; Fruit Ninja web usually requires dragging. I'll support both: hover movement slices? Better require pointerdown drag (mobile friendly) but also allow mouse move while pressed. Add instruction "DRAG TO SLICE". Could also slice on mouse movement regardless for accessibility; but accidental slices. Use pointerdown.

Slicing collision: in pointermove, for each active object, check distance from segment to center. If < radius and not sliced and cooldown, slice. Also maintain combo: slices within 400ms increase multiplier up to 5x.

Game states: idle (start screen), playing, over. Start screen overlay inside activity with "START RUN". Timer 60s. Show HUD: score, timer, lives (3 hearts/bolts), best.

Sound via playTone maybe add noise-like? Could use playTone existing (only if sound on). Add slice tone. Good.

Canvas visual background: dark space dojo with vignette, grid, starfield. CSS background + canvas draws stars. Add "SCRAP RUN" title.

Need to ensure objects spawn within canvas and readable.

- disassembly overlay
